1. My true preference is w > z > x > y
2. However, most applicants seem to favor y > x > w > z

- If I rank y high, I might face more competition at y
- If I rank w high (my true top preference), I have high priority there (rank 1)
- Other students might crowd y, potentially making w easier to get
- By ranking w first, I maximize my chances at my most preferred school
- My high priority at w (rank 1) gives me an advantage
- Even if others rank y higher, my w ranking could be strategically smart

The goal is to balance my true preferences with strategic positioning, considering likely competition and my priority ranks.
